function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single individual—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been observed and studied for millennia. Here’s a quick look at some key figures who helped uncover its secrets:

| Era | Scientist | Contribution |
|-----|-----------|--------------|
| Ancient Greece | **Thales of Miletus** (c. 600 BCE) | First noted static electricity by rubbing amber. |
| 17th–18th Century | **William Gilbert** (1544–1603) | Coined the term *electricus* and distinguished magnetism from static electricity. |
| 18th Century | **Benjamin Franklin** (1706–1790) | Conducted kite experiments, proving lightning is electrical. |
| 18th–19th Century | **Alessandro Volta** (1745–1827) | Invented the voltaic pile, the first chemical battery. |
| 19th Century | **Luigi Galvani** (1737–1798) | Discovered bioelectricity in frog muscles. |
| 19th Century | **Michael Faraday** (1791–1867) | Formulated electromagnetic induction, laying groundwork for generators and motors. |
| 19th Century | **James Clerk Maxwell** (1831–1879) | Unified electricity and magnetism into Maxwell’s equations. |

So while many scientists contributed to our understanding of electricity, it’s more accurate to say that the phenomenon was gradually uncovered over centuries rather than “discovered” by a single person.
